These effects can be caused by alcohol or other drugs, such as some type of sedative and/or tranquiliser.

Stomach aches and vomiting

Some people get stomach aches, especially in the stomach and digestive track, after drinking alcohol. There may be also vomiting.

Irregular heartbeat

After heavy drinking, you may have chest pains, because your heart gets to work overtime to pump the alcohol out of your blood.

Diabetes

Lowered immunity

A decrease in the number of white blood cells makes your body more vulnerable to infections.

Liver problems

Heart disease

Strokes

Alcohol can increase the risk of having a stroke, as it can raise blood pressure and make the blood less viscous, or thick, which can make the blood flow more easily through the blood vessels of the brain, and make it more likely for a blood clot to form.

Decreased sex drive

Alcohol can decrease sexual desire.

Asthma and bronchitis

Dysfunction of the liver function and kidney function

Long-term heavy drinking can also damage the liver and kidneys. Both of these organs usually work by regulating the levels of chemicals in the blood.

Constipation
